title: Arnobius: the first God suffices; his court is honored in him without naming each
source_text: LXIV. Nam ad istam Ethnicorum criminationem sic cum Arnobio respondent. Ad cultum divinitatis obeundum satis est nobis Deus primus, pater rerum ac Dominus, constitutor, moderatorque cunctorum. In hoc omne quod colendum est colimus, quod adorare convenit adoramus, quod obsequium venerationis exposcit, venerationibus promeremur. Cum enim divinitatis ipsius teneamus caput, a quo ipsa divinitas divinorum omnium, quaecunque sunt, ducitur, supervacuum putamus personas ire per singulas, cum & ipsi qui sint, & quae habeant nomina nesciamus, & cujus sint praeterea numeri, neque liquidum, neque comprehensum, neque exploratum habere possimus. Quod postea illustrat illa ipsa ab aulis principum allata similitudine quam eadem hac in re Ethnici usurpabant. Atque, inquit, ut in terrestribus regnis necessitate nulla compellimur, regalibus in familiis constitutos nominatim cum principibus adorare, sed in Regum ipsorum cultu quicquid illis annexum est tacita vi se sentit honorificentia comprehendi; non alia ratione quicunque hi dii sunt, quos esse nobis proponitis, si sunt progenies regia, & principali oriuntur e capite, etiamsi nullos accipiant a nobis nominatim cultus, intelligunt se tamen honorari communiter cum suo Rege, atque in illius venerationibus contineri. Arnob. contra gentes lib. 3. init.
pass_a_gloss: For to that accusation of the Heathen they respond thus with Arnobius. For performing the worship of divinity, the first God is enough for us, father of things and Lord, establisher and governor of all. In him we worship everything which is to be worshipped, what it is fitting to adore we adore, what demands the obedience of veneration, we merit by venerations. For since we hold the head of divinity itself, from which the divinity itself of all divine things, whatever they are, is drawn, we think it superfluous to go through the persons one by one, since we both do not know who they are and what names they have, and moreover of what number they are, we can have it neither clear, nor grasped, nor explored. Which afterwards he illustrates by that very similitude brought from the courts of princes which the Heathen use in this same matter. And, he says, as in earthly kingdoms we are compelled by no necessity to adore by name, together with the princes, those placed in royal families, but in the worship of the Kings themselves whatever is attached to them feels itself comprehended by a tacit force in the honor; in no other way whoever these gods are, whom you propose to us to exist, if they are royal offspring, and arise from the princely head, even if they receive no worships by name from us, they understand nevertheless that they are honored in common with their King, and are contained in his venerations. Arnobius, Against the Nations, book 3, beginning.
pass_b_english: To this pagan charge the early Christians answered with Arnobius: "For the duty of worshiping the divine, the first God is enough for us, the Father of all things and their Lord, the founder and ruler of everything. In him we worship all that is to be worshiped; we adore what it is right to adore; and what calls for the homage of veneration we honor with our veneration."

"Since we hold fast to the head of divinity itself, from which the divinity of all divine beings, whatever they are, is derived, we think it pointless to go through them person by person. We do not know who they are or what names they have, and we cannot have any clear, firm, or tested knowledge of how many of them there are."

He then illustrates this with the very comparison from princes' courts that the pagans used on this point: "In earthly kingdoms no necessity forces us to pay homage by name to the members of the royal family along with the princes. In the honor paid to the kings themselves, everything connected with them feels itself silently included. In the same way, whoever these gods are whom you set before us, if they are royal offspring sprung from the sovereign head, they understand that, even if they receive no worship from us by name, they are honored together with their king and included in the veneration given to him." (Arnobius, Against the Nations, book 3, beginning.)

lemmas.gloss: we hold the head of divinity itself

choices.why: Promereri here means to win or pay due regard; 'merit' would import a theological sense foreign to Arnobius.
